---
title: "Back Pain Basics: Introduction"
---

Back pain is one of the most common complaints encountered in clinical medicine. It is broad, multifactorial, and relevant across many specialties, including primary care, hospitalist medicine, emergency medicine, orthopedics, rheumatology, anesthesiology, and physiatry.

This module is designed to introduce a practical framework for approaching back pain before moving into more specific clinical pain patterns. The goal is to build the foundational anatomy, clinical reasoning, and management approach needed for the modules that follow.

::: {.callout-note}
## By the end of this module, you should be comfortable with:

- [ ] Describing key spine anatomy and common pain generators
- [ ] Organizing back pain into common clinical patterns
- [ ] Taking a focused back pain history
- [ ] Screening for red flags and yellow flags
- [ ] Understanding the role of physical examination
- [ ] Knowing when investigations are and are not useful
- [ ] Choosing an initial management approach
:::
